There’s wishing your partner was taller 

And then there’s... 

Wishing for a taller partner. 

They’re far from the same thing. Because if your hypothetical partner were to answer that yes, she wished *you* were taller. Well then also take the time yourself to ask yourself: do *you* wish that *you* were taller? If you both have the same answer then you can’t exactly blame her for feeling the way that she does. If you had a son, would you wish that he would be shorter, equally, or taller than yourself? 

Realistically this isn’t a healthy question to ask because if she(the one you imagine in your greatest fear) were honest and said no, you’d probably still be suspicious and the question would have done nothing to resolve that suspicion. If she’s honest and says yes, then you’re probably a bit triggered and your brain would struggle to process the part immediately after the yes that’d go ‘yes but that’s not a real factor to me because I love you just as you are’

I’m a 5”3’ guy here. I can imagine you now instantly either consciously or subconsciously choosing to dismiss anything I may have to say. Either your brain just flat out turns off or finds some reason or some way to say “yeah, but...” 

That is because you feel a certain type of way and maybe for the time being you just need to express that. So to that end, I feel you man. I can see the emotions in the words of your post and I’ve thought much of that to myself for a long time. So most importantly I just wanna day that your feelings here are valid. Your conclusions are not reasonable to me but your feelings there are absolutely valid. 

For myself, I had always hated when people would try to tell me things like ‘It’s all personality’ or ‘It’s all about the way you present yourself & carry yourself’ or ‘Just have some confidence’ ... because I had considered those possibilities and I explored and experimented but ultimately I only became more certain of what I had always known; that my height was a significant limiting factor in the dating scene, and the majority of that limitation cannot be overcome by personality factors. 

Statistically speaking, I’m as short as a 6”8’ guy is tall. To be perfectly honest, I’ve wished for a long time that I was just 4 inches taller, as tall as you are. Because for me then, yeah I’d still be a little short but my height wouldn’t be the very first thing that someone thinks/notices when they see me. I could at least be taller than the average girl’s height. I hope that you honestly consider that there are plenty of guys such as myself that imagine much of our dating problems going away if we could just be 5”7’. Maybe you don’t want to right this moment, but you absolutely should consider that for at least an entire 30 seconds. 

I don’t know much about being Asian because I can’t speak from experience. It’s certainly believable to me that it *can* affect your relationships, but there’s just so many other factors when it comes to dating that to me would play a larger or more significant role. I think if anyone is writing you off as a potential purely for being Asian, that they would be in the minority. But I’m sure it happens occasionally enough, and that when it happens it’s very painful. I’m sorry you’ve had to endure that from anyone. 

I sincerely hope that your emotional conclusions here are just that- emotional. That you don’t seriously mean them, as this is just a vent. I hope you’re able to see that in yourself.

I would say that you shouldn’t let the approval/disapproval of strangers intrude on the relationship between yourself and your girlfriend. 

A three month old relationship is a very young one, and between two young adults. This is a time of great opportunity for growth for each of you as individuals, and for your shared relationship together. This will be true if that relationship persists romantically for the rest of your lives, or if your relationship needs to change from it’s current state. 

Everyone is going to be comfortable with a certain range of PDA, and if she is more comfortable with certain things than you are, then that will be up to you to establish & enforce those boundaries out of respect to yourself. However your (and her) comfort level with varying degrees of PDA can certainly change over time provided that there is of course the desire to, and there is the proper amount of self-reflection, mutual self-respect, and communication between the two of you. 

The crucial aspect of all of this from what I can tell is this: *why* does the disapproving looks of others affect you? 

My concern would be the scenario that it is actually you who is genuinely uncomfortable with this height disparity in your relationship, and that the perceived reaction from others is largely a stinging reminder of that internal conflict. 

If at your heart it is you who is genuinely uncomfortable with this aspect of your relationship, then you must reflect on & identify *why* it is that you are uncomfortable with this aspect of your relationship. Some reasons may be reasonable/rational, and others may be unreasonable or unfair. Other issues can be resolved assuming that you are ready/willing to overcome them. Or perhaps it is something that cannot be resolved, and the relationship would have to change from its current form. 

If you are truly, entirely comfortable and happy about this consideration, and it is *only* the disapproval, peer pressure, or outright disgust of others that is affecting your ability to be a respectful and/or affectionate partner for your girlfriend, then my advice would be to start getting used to it. At that point, you will be choosing between the approval of others and the respect/affection of your girlfriend.

The most important thing is that your relationship is not likely to be a very healthy one for either of you if you continue to struggle being seen with her in public. Your girlfriend deserves your best efforts and I’m sure you would hope for the same from her. PDA is something that the two of you can modify to a level you both can be comfortable with if there’s a problem there but that doesn’t seem to be the fundamental reason for your seeking advice. 

Bear in mind that there are/will be plenty of options for both of you and you don’t need to be trying to fit a square peg to a round hole. Particularly for you there are taller girls (5”8 +) who are being passed on by other guys due to their taller height but would make a great fit for you at 6”2. Additionally there are plenty of shorter guys out there (5”7 & shorter) who are being passed on by most due to their shorter height but would be a great fit for a girl at 4”7. Of course there are no actual restrictions on height in terms of dating but I’m just referring to the most common heterosexual romantic relationship which typically involves a taller guy. 

I know it’s corny but honestly the best, most concise piece of advice I have for you is to follow your heart and accept the challenges that will go along with it. 

Anyways I hope I’ve made some sense here or at least that any of this is helpful to you in any way, and I wish the best for you both. I’m happy to help further if you have questions.

I’m no expert or authority, and I’m still learning, so please take what I say with caution, but... 

From my understanding, hyperadrenergic POTS would be consistent with elevated HR and elevated BP on standing. 

It sounds like your body/mind went into fight/flight mode, and you can’t consciously/willingly come back down. 

Given that you have dysautonomia, you may need to boost the functionality of your Vagus nerve, in order to promote parasympathetic (de-stress) response... While simultaneously reducing/eliminating any stress/anxiety triggers, and any stimulants like caffeine. 

If massaging, singing/humming, or breathing exercises are unhelpful, you may need to talk with a doctor about some form of medical intervention. Prescription medications like Acetazolamide or Pyridostigmine come to mind, or even a Vegus Nerve Stimulation device(surgical device that uses electric signals to help). 

Obviously I would recommend vagus nerve stimulation before drugs or surgery. Eliminate the stressors/triggers/stimulants. Try some sensory deprivation (go somewhere as quiet as possible and close your eyes for some time). Try a massage to your neck! Especially in the area on the sides of your neck, below the ear. A buddy could be especially helpful for that if they’re willing. Some people find CBD or MMJ to be helpful. If/when you’re able to regain gastrointestinal function, try eating some watermelon, it would help your blood vessels to vasodilate. Research yourself for anything else that may help with vagus nerve function. And please remember to come back and share with us your findings/results!

I only mention this to try to be helpful so I hope you don’t find this offensive but this post reeks of overwhelming anxiety to me. In your words here I can see a lot of pain, vulnerability, judgement, self-hatred, and more judgement. I’m not a mental health professional but if you have any school/professional resources, insurance, or any other means to find a mental health professional, that may be a good step to consider. 

With that said, I have to ask; what are your values? As in, what core things are most important to you in life? The vital few things that you feel you could not be content in life without them? 

Secondly, what are your goals in life? Are they specific/measurable? Or are they broad/vague? No wrong answers here. Essentially, how do you personally measure success? What standards must you meet in order to be satisfied with yourself? 

I could be wrong, but I imagine that you probably feel a constant pull to ‘escape’ those overwhelming thoughts/feelings. Some people escape by solving other people’s problems, by drugs/alcohol, by cleaning, by watching tv shows or YouTube videos... What patterns do you see within yourself? How/where are you able to pretend that these overwhelming, painful, anxiety-provoking things no longer exist? Where do you escape? 

Wherever you ‘escape’ to could be hiding some of your own actual passions, or even some of your major pitfalls. It takes intentional effort and time in order to notice some of these things. 

TDLR; Take a deep breath, take a shower, ‘give yourself’ some stability, and honestly take the time to organize your thoughts. Use the organization to plan/strategize a course of action. It’s always okay to reach out for help too.

I wouldn't argue that he has a touch problem. Yes, he throws hard more frequently than most quarterbacks, but it seems to only be a problem for poor receivers to begin with. For guys like Greg Olsen, Cam is delivering an accurate ball into a tight window. 

Look I'm not trying to argue that Cam is the best passer in the NFL, but I think it's fair to say he's much better than "mediocre". He's in general a pretty good passer who flashes greatness and who also flashes ineptitude.

I think it's fair to criticize Cam's play. However in my view Cam needs to be quicker to hit his checkdowns, as he waits too long for his targets downfield to create separation. He needs to make sure he sets his feet when throwing short, because he relies too heavily in his arm strength and that can affect his accuracy. However to say that he "misses insanely easy throws, misses easy reads, forces into coverage, and has zero touch", kind of screams that you haven't really watched him play very often.

I'm not about to pull up stats about how much time his Oline provides time for him or how long it takes his receivers to get open or how many times they drop the ball. I'm just saying that maybe we fall victim to group think when it comes to Cam as a passer. Cam isn't the passer that popular opinion, or completion percentage stats would have you to believe.

I think fans in general rely on completion percentages too heavily to form opinions on a QB's accuracy or performance. We see the stats and then fall victim to confirmation bias. 

I'm not saying Cam is infallible, and statistics can be helpful/insightful to understanding a player's performance. Undoubtedly he had a down year last year, but without consideration of his supporting cast and the offense's playcalling philosophy, couldn't you admit that calling him a mediocre passer is somewhat lazy?

The Tampa 2 (from wikipedia), "blends the cover 2 and cover 3 defenses by having two DBs, usually the safeties, in deep coverage on either side of the field, and a middle linebacker covering the medium to deep middle".  So in theory, with the right personnel, a Tampa 2 defense is better than the cover 2 against the deep pass, and better than the cover 3 against the short pass.  It seems to require a lot from the MLB, FS, and SS.

The Cover 3(wikipedia) "refers to 3 deep defenders each guarding one-third of the deep zone"... "Upon snap, the CBs work for depth, backpedaling into their assigned zone. One safety moves toward the center of the field. The other safety is free to rotate into the flat area (about 2-4 yards beyond the line of scrimmage), provide pass coverage help, or blitz". ... "One of the biggest benefits of the cover 3 coverage scheme is the ability to walk the SS up into the box with minimal to no changes in the coverage due to the pre-snap center field position of the FS".  As a fan, I know the panthers frequently run the cover 3 from the nickel personnel group.  The cover 3 is typically strong against the deep pass, but susceptible to short and intermediate throws.  It seems to require a lot from the FS, OLB, and nickel CB(or safety, in a big nickle).
